Admissions: Application deadline for Fall semester is January 15. Early Decision deadline is November 1. Application fee is $75 (fee waivers available for qualifying students). Required materials: transcripts, SAT/ACT scores (test-optional for 2024-2025), two recommendation letters, personal essay.

Acceptance Rate: The university accepts approximately 23% of applicants. Middle 50% SAT: 1380-1520. Middle 50% ACT: 31-34. Average high school GPA: 3.85. Holistic review considers academics, extracurriculars, essays, and demonstrated interest.

Tuition and Fees (2024-2025): Undergraduate tuition: $52,000 per year. Room and board: $16,500. Books and supplies: $1,200 estimated. Student fees: $800. Total estimated cost: $70,500 per year. Graduate tuition varies by program.

Financial Aid: 65% of students receive financial aid. Average aid package: $38,000. Need-blind admissions for domestic students. CSS Profile and FAFSA required. Merit scholarships range from $10,000 to full tuition. Work-study positions available on campus.

Scholarships: Presidential Scholarship: Full tuition for top applicants. Dean's Scholarship: $25,000/year for academic excellence. Diversity Scholarship: $15,000/year promoting inclusive campus. STEM Scholarship: $20,000/year for science and engineering majors. Apply by February 1 for priority consideration.

Housing: Freshmen required to live on campus. Housing options: traditional dorms, suite-style, apartment-style. Room selection based on deposit date. Average room cost: $8,000/year. Meal plans required for dorm residents, starting at $5,500/year.

Dining: 5 dining halls across campus. Meal plan options: Unlimited, 14 meals/week, 10 meals/week. Flex dollars accepted at all campus eateries. Dietary accommodations available (vegetarian, vegan, halal, kosher, gluten-free). Late night dining until 2am at Student Center.

Academic Calendar: Fall semester: August 25 - December 15. Spring semester: January 15 - May 10. Summer sessions available. Reading days before finals. Winter break: 4 weeks. Spring break: 1 week in March.

Registration: Course registration opens April 1 (Fall) and November 1 (Spring). Priority registration for seniors, then juniors, sophomores, freshmen. Waitlist available for full courses. Add/drop period: first two weeks of semester. Advisor approval required for some courses.

Majors and Minors: 80+ undergraduate majors across 6 colleges. Popular majors: Computer Science, Biology, Economics, Psychology, Engineering. Double majors allowed. Minors require 5-6 courses. Undeclared students must declare major by end of sophomore year.

Computer Science Major: 12 required courses plus electives. Core: Intro to CS, Data Structures, Algorithms, Systems, Theory of Computation. Specializations: AI/ML, Systems, Security, HCI. Senior capstone project required. Internship strongly encouraged.

Study Abroad: 200+ programs in 60 countries. Semester, year, and summer options. Financial aid applies to approved programs. Credits transfer back. Apply one year in advance. Most popular destinations: London, Paris, Tokyo, Sydney, Barcelona.

Research Opportunities: 70% of undergraduates participate in research. SURF (Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship): $5,000 stipend. Faculty mentorship in all disciplines. Present at annual Undergraduate Research Symposium. Research credits can count toward major.

Internships: Career Center helps find internships. 85% of students complete at least one internship. Average internship pay: $22/hour. Academic credit available (optional). Companies recruiting on campus: Google, Microsoft, Goldman Sachs, NASA, NIH.

Career Services: Resume and cover letter reviews. Mock interviews with industry professionals. Career fairs each semester (Fall, Spring). Alumni networking events. Job board with 5,000+ postings. Lifetime access for alumni.

Graduate School Preparation: Pre-law advising available. Pre-med committee writes evaluations. GRE prep courses offered. 40% of graduates attend graduate school within 5 years. Strong placement at top law, medical, and PhD programs.

Library: Main library open 24/7 during semester. 3 million print volumes, 500,000 e-books. 200 study rooms (reserve online). Interlibrary loan for materials we don't have. Research librarians available for consultations. Printing: $0.10/page black and white, $0.25/page color.

Health Services: Student Health Center on campus. Free basic medical visits. Pharmacy with discounted medications. Mental health counseling: 10 free sessions per year. After-hours nurse hotline. Health insurance required (student plan available: $2,500/year).

Counseling Center: Free confidential counseling for all students. Individual and group therapy. Crisis support 24/7. Workshops on stress, anxiety, time management. Psychiatric services available. Waitlist may apply during peak times.

Recreation and Fitness: Two fitness centers with modern equipment. Olympic swimming pool. Rock climbing wall. Intramural sports: 20+ options. Club sports: 40+ teams. Group fitness classes included with student fees. Outdoor adventure program with hiking, camping, skiing trips.

Student Organizations: 400+ registered student organizations. Student Government Association. Cultural organizations, academic clubs, performing arts. Greek life: 15 fraternities, 12 sororities (15% participation). Start a new org with 5 members and faculty advisor.

Campus Safety: 24/7 campus police. Blue light emergency phones across campus. SafeWalk escort service after dark. Anonymous tip line. Crime alerts sent via email and text. Residence halls secured with card access.

Parking: Freshman not permitted to have cars. Parking permits: $800/year for commuters, $1,200/year for residents. Limited availability - lottery system. Free weekend parking in visitor lots. Bicycle registration free. Bike share program available.

Transportation: Free campus shuttle running 7am-midnight. Bus pass included in student fees (city-wide). Zipcar and bike share on campus. Airport shuttle during breaks ($30 one-way). Closest airport: 20 miles away.

IT Services: Free WiFi campus-wide. Microsoft Office 365 free for students. 1TB OneDrive storage. Computer labs in library and academic buildings. Laptop loaner program. IT help desk in Student Center. Software discounts through campus store.

Disability Services: Register with Office of Accessibility. Accommodations: extended test time, note-takers, assistive technology. Accessible housing available. Sign language interpreters upon request. Documentation required (submit 4+ weeks before semester).

International Students: 15% of student body from 90+ countries. International Student Office provides visa support. English language support through Writing Center. Cultural adjustment programming. Work authorization guidance (CPT, OPT). Airport pickup for new students.

Veterans Services: Yellow Ribbon school - full tuition covered for eligible veterans. Dedicated Veterans Center on campus. Priority registration. Credit for military training. Veteran peer mentors. VA benefits certification on campus.

Graduation Requirements: 120 credits for bachelor's degree. Core curriculum: 40 credits. Major requirements: 40-50 credits. Electives: remaining credits. Minimum 2.0 GPA required. Residency requirement: last 30 credits at university. Apply for graduation one semester before completion.
